title: Running through 8/15  📸 Geve Penn #theatre #performance #arts #hidden...
transcript: In a busted former sweater factory in South Queens is a new performance venue where they're doing a bizarre, unfinished 19th century German play. From the theatre company Adult Film comes this rare revival of Woyzeck, the inaugural production in this new venue, Modern Sweater, which at least right now, has a well worn, unfinished, and not especially inviting aura about it. But that's kind of fitting for this play, which was discovered in a drawer decades after the playwright's untimely death at age 23 and had to be cobbled together from multiple unfinished drafts. So much so that even the order of the scenes is up to interpretation from version to version. It tells the story of a soldier named Woyzeck who's being dehumanized and exploited by his army captain and a scientist doing experiments on him, all of which drives him increasingly to insanity. It's grotesque and unsettling at times, which this production leans into with its staging and visuals, making a very distinct aesthetic impression that's equal parts nightmarish and whimsical. This production also utilizes two live musicians who punctuate the action with songs and underscoring, which contributes to that sense of whimsy and even a darkly comical edge. I remember studying this play in my freshman year of college, but almost nothing about the plot or themes, so it was kind of like experiencing it for the first time. It leaves a lot to chew on in terms of its commentary about how this common man Is sort of being sacrificed for what these forces might argue is the greater good of society. Even though there is an overarching narrative, it does still have a sort of fragmented and disorienting feel to it. But hard to know how much of that is the unfinished nature of the play versus the playwright deliberately alienating the audience. Overall, I think I find it more interesting academically than dramatically. But I do think this production did some cool stuff with it.
